scope: Fresh complete rigid front-column, rear-base and rear-over-core closing intervals on the current physical quadrant STLs. Pump and cap admission are additionally checked with back-top separated, pump joints/leads disconnected and cap released; only their own intended seated interfaces are omitted. Cross-parent flexible spans and the loose pump inlet elbow and its short inlet link are connected through the uncovered funnel aperture after closure. This establishes nominal rigid travel, not flexure force or flexible handling.
assembly_prerequisites: Keep the pump suction elbow and short inlet link loose during the populated rear approach; complete their round joints through the uncovered funnel opening after closure.
Dress cross-parent flexible tube spans after positioning the rigid quadrants.
Separate back-top and disconnect pump joints/leads before pump service; release and remove the continuous cap before lifting the pump.

current_complete_motion_reading.method: Complete translation intervals certified from triangle-surface distances using the 1-Lipschitz translation bound. Broad-phase separation uses complete swept AABBs. Any surface contact or unresolved interval remains a witness for native follow-up. Cross-parent tubes and the loose pump inlet elbow and its short inlet link are connected after closure through the funnel opening, per the accepted rotating-joint assembly sequence. This does not infer flexible handling or printed force.

assembly_prerequisite_scope_correction.instruction: Keep the pump suction elbow and its short quarter-inch inlet link loose while positioning back-top. Make these round joints through the uncovered funnel opening after closure.

All remaining pair certificates use the exact same geometry, translation intervals and printed STL hashes; removing this link introduces no new pair or altered path.

limits: Nominal rigid translation geometry and triangle-distance bounds. Released hook flexure, physical force, hose dressing and printed support cleanup need their actual article evidence.
